description: IGEL 2024, the Inventory of Global Emissions by Launchers for 2024, is a launch-by-launch inventory of rocket emissions for the calendar year, covering 223 launches and 26 launch vehicles, about 95.6 percent of the propellant used by orbital launches, plus four suborbital Starship test flights. A team at the German Aerospace Center with TU Braunschweig released it in July 2026. It combines launch vehicle models, reconstructed trajectories and engine-specific exhaust compositions with altitude-dependent post-combustion parameters, giving 110.5 kt of primary exhaust and 130.9 kt of final emissions of carbon dioxide, water vapour, carbon monoxide, nitrogen species, alumina, black carbon and chlorine compounds. It holds two global NetCDF inventories at 1 degree and 1 km vertical steps up to 80 km, monthly, per-launch three-dimensional profiles keyed by COSPAR launch tags, exhaust indices for 36 engine types, a launch list and vehicle data; a separate generator builds custom inventories. Coverage is global. Format and access: a 90 MB zip on Zenodo, found through a web search, not a Zenodo search. Licence: CC-BY-4.0; free. Caveats: vehicle and trajectory models are withheld as sensitive, and exhaust measurements are scarce. It supports environmental impact assessments of space launch for climate studies. Related catalogue records are the 2020-2022 rocket launch and re-entry emissions inventory and DLR's reference rocket engine exhaust datasets.
